skill.name: competitor-tracker
skill.description: Analyze competitor influencer programs by tracking partner rosters, campaign tactics, content patterns, performance estimates, and opportunity gaps.
skill.summary: Track rival creator partnerships and turn campaign patterns into market opportunities.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown links, prompt examples, connector labels, or project metadata. I confirmed two explicit Python connector command templates as medium external-command risks because they run local scripts with user-supplied competitor or partner values. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running connector commands, sanitize competitor names and handles, and prefer structured tool calls when available.

remediation.issue: Optional API key handling for YouTube connector
remediation.suggestion: State that API keys must never be printed, saved in reports, or passed to unrelated tools.

remediation.issue: Relative documentation links trigger static path alarms
remediation.suggestion: Keep relative links for documentation only, and avoid using traversal paths in executable command examples.

content.value_statement: Competitor influencer activity is hard to compare across channels and campaigns. This skill builds a structured view of partner rosters, campaign tactics, performance estimates, and open opportunities.
actual_capabilities: Defines competitor sets, platforms, time periods, and focus areas.
Builds partner rosters with handles, platforms, follower counts, partnership types, and durations.
Breaks down recent campaigns by timeline, tier mix, content type, CTA, hashtag, and estimated spend.
Reviews content formats, themes, messages, hashtags, and creative direction.
Produces side-by-side comparisons and ranked opportunity lists.
Labels performance and spend figures as estimates.
limitations: It depends on public posts, user-provided data, or available analytics tools.
Performance, spend, and share-of-voice numbers are estimates unless sources provide verified figures.
It does not discover new creators outside competitor-focused opportunities.
Platform API limits and missing handles can reduce coverage.

use_cases.title: Benchmark rival creator programs
use_cases.description: Compare competitor partner rosters, active platforms, tier mix, campaign cadence, and estimated spend against your own program.

use_cases.title: Find campaign gaps
use_cases.description: Identify formats, niches, platforms, and creator types that competitors underuse, then rank the best opportunities.

use_cases.title: Prepare market briefs
use_cases.description: Summarize competitor campaigns, content themes, and likely performance into a report for planning discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Track one competitor
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single rival.
prompt_templates.prompt: Track influencer marketing activity for [competitor] on [platforms] during [time period]. Include partner roster, campaign themes, and estimated performance.

prompt_templates.title: Compare several rivals
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [your brand] with [competitor 1], [competitor 2], and [competitor 3]. Show partner tiers, content formats, cadence, and opportunity gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a campaign window
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review around launches or seasons.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review competitor influencer campaigns around [launch or season]. Break down creators, platforms, hashtags, CTAs, estimated spend, and what worked.

prompt_templates.title: Build a strategic report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a competitive intelligence report for [category]. Include partner rosters, strategy comparison, share-of-voice estimates, risks, and ranked recommendations.

output_examples.input: Compare Glossier, Fenty Beauty, and Rare Beauty across TikTok and Instagram.
output_examples.output: A market brief with partner rosters, platform mix, campaign themes, estimated reach, content patterns, and ranked whitespace opportunities.

output_examples.input: Track one competitor before our product launch.
output_examples.output: A launch-focused report showing recent creator partners, active messages, likely campaign timing, and gaps your brand can use.

output_examples.input: Find creators competitors stopped using in the last quarter.
output_examples.output: A shortlist of former competitor partners, evidence notes, possible availability, and next-step recommendations for outreach review.

best_practices: Provide competitor names, platforms, market category, and the analysis period.
Separate verified facts from estimates, especially for spend and performance.
Review the opportunity list with brand fit, audience safety, and exclusivity checks.
anti_patterns: Do not treat estimates as verified performance data.
Do not use the skill when you only need broad creator discovery.
Do not compare competitors without defining the market, platform, and time period.

faq.question: What does this skill track?
faq.answer: It tracks competitor creator partners, campaign tactics, content strategy, estimated performance, and opportunity gaps.

faq.question: Can it find new creators for my brand?
faq.answer: It can surface untapped or former competitor creators. Broad creator discovery belongs in a separate discovery workflow.

faq.question: Does it require paid data tools?
faq.answer: No. It can work from user-provided data and public sources, but analytics connectors can improve coverage.

faq.question: How should estimates be handled?
faq.answer: All reach, spend, EMV, and share-of-voice estimates should be labeled as estimates unless a source verifies them.

faq.question: Which platforms can it compare?
faq.answer: It can compare platforms named by the user, such as Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or other relevant channels.

faq.question: What is the main output?
faq.answer: The main output is a competitor intelligence report with comparison tables, campaign notes, and ranked recommendations.
